messages:
alice: Quick heads-up — observed a microburst this morning where a stream of tiny requests spun off the coalesce window and created a 350-450ms tail for small interactive calls. Dumping notes here.

ben: Hmm. Was that the pattern where requests arrive just after the window cut and then 'slipstream' through single-request execution? I saw similar traces yesterday. :thinking:

carla: Yep, looks like slipstreaming — a lot of 1-3 token requests that don't join batches and contend on the same slots. Impacts small-request latency but improves throughput for large batches. Tradeoff.

dmitri: Two hypotheses: (1) admission policy is too greedy for tiny requests, letting them preempt fill; (2) KV cache eviction / headroom handshake is starving fastpath because of late joins. We should instrument headroom per-tenant.

eva: Agreed. Minimal mitigation ideas: add a short-lived "slipstream" lane for tiny requests with soft reservation credits and preemption window. That keeps them off the main coalescer but yields bounded tails.

carla: Important we keep fairness. Slipstream should consume credit buckets that replenish slowly (so it can't DOS). Also preempt only when slot idle < X ms.

ben: Prototype suggestion: config + admission check in scheduler. Something like:
```yaml
slipstream:
  enabled: true
  max_concurrent: 8
  refill_rate_per_sec: 2
  preempt_threshold_ms: 8
  max_tenant_fraction: 0.05
```
This keeps lanes tiny and bounded.

alice: Nice. What about KV cache interaction? If slipstream bypasses coalesce, it may not install KV entries, leading to repeated upstream work.

dmitri: Exactly. Two options: (A) allow slipstream to warm a light-weight KV cache entry (metadata-only), or (B) accept higher model compute for small fastpath but throttle if misses exceed X/s. Option A needs a safe handshake so eviction doesn't race.

carla: Option A seems preferable for latency-sensitive flows. Implement a write-through metadata key with TTL = 500ms so big batches still populate full KV state later. Small memory overhead.

ben: We need a preemptive eviction signal in the lease protocol: when a batch that will install full KV arrives, it can mark overlapping slipstream metadata as "stale" so subsequent small requests wait briefly and then join batch. Otherwise we get double-work.

alice: Telemetry requirements: per-tenant slipstream hits, misses, double-exec count, avg tail latency for 1-5 token requests. Also track how often slipstream consumes >max_tenant_fraction.

eva: I'll add metrics and dashboards. Proposed alert: slipstream double-exec rate > 0.5% for 5min -> roll back.

dmitri: Concern: complexity of handshake + lease changes. Alternative lightweight experiment: node-local slipstream lane that is ephemeral and can't influence global KV. Simpler, but less cache benefit.

carla: Let's A/B test: rollout node-local slipstream for 24h on 10% of capacity, compare latency tail and extra token cost. If good, iterate to metadata-assisted mode.

ben: Also add a queue-shaper rule: if coalesce window occupancy > 70% for last 30s, disable slipstream on that host to preserve batch efficiency.

alice: Plan sounds sensible. Action items:
- ev: add metrics + dashboard (eva)
- ben: implement node-local slipstream lane + config toggle (2d)
- carla/dmitri: sketch metadata write-through TTL and eviction handshake (1d)
- ops-bot: schedule canary 10% tomorrow 08:00 UTC

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: eng-runtime/nodepool-3 10% at 2026-03-22T08:00:00Z. :rocket:

eva: Will add dashboards and a short runbook.

alice: Thanks all — let's sync after the 24h canary. :) :thumbsup:
